title: TTM Category A: Roadway Foundations & Safety
description: Essential safety protocols, hazard identification, and live-lane awareness under CoPTTM and NZGTTM operational frameworks.

units.title: 1. Fundamental Safety & Legal Duties
units.content: All personnel operating on or adjacent to live carriageways must wear high-visibility Level 2/3 apparel. Site visibility, risk mitigation, and continuous perimeter monitoring are compulsory baseline requirements before placing equipment.

units.title: 2. Buffer Zones & Longitudinal Separation
units.content: A buffer zone provides lateral and longitudinal clearance between live traffic lanes and the active work area. Longitudinal buffers must remain completely unobstructed by work vehicles, tools, or personnel at all times.

units.title: 3. Dynamic Site Assessment & Spot Hazard Checks
units.content: When weather or site conditions degrade sight distance below minimum operating tolerances, the STMS must enact modified speed limits or call an immediate operational pause until safety parameters are restored.

questions.prompt: What is the primary operational rule regarding longitudinal buffer zones?
options: They can be used for staging small utility vehicles
They must remain entirely clear of workers, plant, and equipment
They only apply during night operations
They can store excess safety cones
questions.explanation: Longitudinal buffer zones must always remain completely unobstructed to safeguard the work zone.

questions.prompt: Who holds immediate operational authority to pause works if site sight distance drops below standard?
questions.explanation: The STMS / Safety Supervisor has direct responsibility and authority to halt work if safety thresholds are breached.

questions.prompt: What minimum high-visibility garment standard is mandatory on live carriageway operations?
options: Standard street clothing with reflector bands
Level 2 / Level 3 High-Visibility TTMC-W Compliant Apparel
questions.explanation: Compliant Level 2 / 3 TTMC-W apparel is mandatory across all active roadway work environments.

title: TTM Category B: Taper Geometry & Sign Placement
description: Calculations for approach tapers, lateral shift rates, sign spacing intervals, and delineation cone placement.

units.title: 1. Taper Ratios & Speed Environments
units.content: Taper lengths directly correlate with permanent speed thresholds. A 100 km/h environment demands longer transition tapers to allow drivers adequate reaction and deceleration distance.

units.title: 2. Sign Sequencing and Sight Distances
units.content: Advance warning signs must be positioned with unobstructed sightlines, accounting for vertical crests, horizontal bends, and roadside foliage.

questions.prompt: Why are longer tapers required in higher speed environments (e.g. 100 km/h)?
options: To use up extra cones stored on the truck
To afford motorists sufficient decision and lateral merging time
To restrict lane width for bicycle traffic only
Taper length does not change with speed
questions.explanation: High-speed corridors require increased transition distances for safe, controlled lateral merging.
